policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'go thou' renders the 2fs pronoun; qere אַתְּ and ketiv אתי are spelling variants of the same pronoun and the English cannot distinguish them. No mapped note. Base qere fallback carries the projection.

ASV main text 'say unto him, Thou shalt surely recover' renders qere ל֖וֹ ('to him'); the mapped textual_variant note 'Another reading is, say, Thou shalt not recover' identifies ketiv לא as the alternative the ASV did not follow in its text.

ASV 'eight years' is the idiomatic English for the numeral phrase whether the noun is plural qere שָׁנִים or singular ketiv שנה; the English does not distinguish. No mapped note. Base qere fallback carries the projection.
